title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages. π is a group and ρ acts on π with order n. Equation (8) is the 'équation des lacets' g ρ(g) ⋯ ρ^{n-1}(g) = 1. Its solutions g correspond to the lifts ρ'_g = g ρ0 of order n in the semidirect product π̃ = π ⋊ Z/n, where ρ0 is a fixed base lift. Two solutions are identified under ρ-conjugation g ~ α g ρ(α)^{-1}. The classes of solutions are therefore the non-abelian cohomology set H^1(Z/n, π). Equivalently, they are the π-conjugacy classes of splittings of 1→π→π̃→Z/n→1.

The previous page noted that writing a solution as g = α ρ(α)^{-1} with α only in π̃ (rather than π) is no longer unambiguous. On this page Grothendieck generalises the setting.

- **Ambient extension.** He takes an extension (20) 1→π→E→G→1 and an element ρ ∈ G of order n, i.e. an embedding (21) Z/n ↪ G. Then π̃ is the inverse image of Z/n in E, so the extension π̃ is pulled back from E along Z/n ↪ G (the marginal NB). His motivating example is π = π_{0,3}, G = S_3, E = an extension of S_3 by π_{0,3}, with ρ the 3-cycle.
- **Which conjugations preserve lifts.** For α ∈ E, int(α)(ρ') still lies over ρ if and only if the image α̇ commutes with ρ in G.
- **The subgroup E_ρ.** Hence (22): E_ρ = {α ∈ E : [α̇, ρ] = 1}, the inverse image of the centraliser G^ρ. It contains π̃.
- **The action.** E_ρ acts by conjugation on the set of order-n lifts of ρ. In terms of solutions this is (23): α ρ'_g α^{-1} = ρ'_{α g ρ(α)^{-1}}, i.e. (24) the twisted action Θ(α): g ↦ α g ρ(α)^{-1}.
- **Check.** α g ρ0 α^{-1} = α g (ρ0 α^{-1} ρ0^{-1}) ρ0 = (α g ρ(α)^{-1}) ρ0. The factor α g ρ(α)^{-1} lies in π exactly when [α, ρ0] ∈ π, i.e. when α ∈ E_ρ.
- **Effect on classes.** Since π acts trivially on classes, this action permutes the π-ρ-conjugacy classes of solutions of (8), i.e. H^1(Z/n, π). The next page completes this: E_ρ is an extension (25) of G^ρ by π, and G^ρ acts on H^1(Z/n, π).
- **Purpose.** The next page uses this action to decide when a solution g can be written in the 'standard form' α ρ(α)^{-1} with α ∈ E_ρ rather than α ∈ π. This happens exactly when [g] lies in the G^ρ-orbit of the trivial class [1].

The purpose is to understand the solutions of the loop equation (torsion elements / splittings over a cyclic subgroup) in π_{0,3}-type extensions. This bears on the conjugacy classes of finite-order elements in anabelian fundamental groups attached to M_{0,n} / Teichmüller-type extensions.
errors: No mathematical error. One small imprecision: the parenthetical '(i.e. s'il satisfait ρ'^n = 1)' conflates 'ρ' lies over ρ' with 'ρ' lifts ρ with order n'. Only the latter gives a solution of (8); the intended meaning is clear from context.

ideas.what: Classes of solutions of the twisted 'loop equation' g ρ(g)⋯ρ^{n-1}(g) = 1, modulo g ~ α g ρ(α)^{-1}, identified with conjugacy classes of splittings / order-n lifts.
ideas.modern_name: Non-abelian cohomology H^1(Z/n, π); classification of complements/splittings
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Serre, Cohomologie galoisienne, ch. I §5; Borel–Serre)

ideas.what: Given an extension 1→π→E→G→1 and ρ ∈ G of order n, the inverse image E_ρ of the centraliser C_G(ρ) acts by twisted conjugation g ↦ α g ρ(α)^{-1} on solutions. This induces an action of C_G(ρ) on H^1(<ρ>, π).
ideas.modern_name: Action of the centraliser (normaliser) on H^1 of a subgroup; outer action on classes of torsion lifts / sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in group cohomology / non-abelian cohomology

ideas.what: Application to π = π_{0,3} with G = S_3 and ρ a 3-cycle, aimed at torsion in anabelian (Teichmüller-type) extensions.
ideas.modern_name: Torsion / finite subgroups in profinite mapping class groups and Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, Longue Marche); later Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, etc.
ideas.where_published: Theme related to Esquisse d'un programme / La Longue Marche (finite subgroups and inertia), unsure of this precise formulation

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up a routine piece of non-abelian group cohomology: the centraliser action on H^1(Z/n, π) via the extension E_ρ. It is careful and correct but standard. Its interest lies only in its role within Grothendieck's study of the loop equation for π_{0,3}.
transcription_corrections: '(donc ρ' ∈ Ẽ)' should read '(donc ρ' ∈ π̃)'.
Marginal NB: it should read roughly 'NB l'extension π̃ [est induite] par l'inclusion Z/nZ ↪ G' (π̃ is the pullback of E along Z/n ↪ G).
The line '(3) [?] (20) donne' appears to be a renumbering mark for (20) followed by an abandoned 'donne'; it is not an equation (3).
The final line 'Elle aura sur E_ρ^ρ' most likely reads '[Ici] E_ρ aura' (continuing on the next page with 'une structure d'extension'); the superscript is not part of the notation.
In (23), the subscript on ρ' is g: ρ'_g, not ρ'_j.
